title: update gather/spread to pivot_wider/pivot_longer
description:
addressed issue #27 

Contribution:

- updates the labels on tidyr::gather() and tidyr::spread() to be up to date with tidyverse recommendations

Issues:

- Ideally I'd like the labels to say names_to = "key", values_to = "val" and the reverse, but this forces the labels onto two lines and that makes the animation jumpy (because of the resizing of the main plot).
- I kept the original spreading and gathering code for the transitions because when I originally updated them, it made the gif blink a lot and I'm not sure the root cause of that issue.  
- Naming conventions may be funky for the new plot names, I'd take a close look at them to make sure them match stylistically. 

Thanks for your awesome tidyexplain package!

title: Add framework for animation options (fixed)
description:
**Fixed version of #18**

This is an extension of #16 and that will help us move towards resolving #17.

It sets up a framework for creating, setting and transporting the animation options that may need to be passed through several helper functions to get to the final `animate_plot()` or `static_plot()` call.

It also lets

1. The user set animation options for the current session, much like `theme_set()` in ggplot2
2. Us create "default" animation options by verb family
3. Us define or change the global defaults easily from one place.

I've created a more detailed explanation in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/gadenbuie/c46c9d65de531f2dfa65c7a6a6e893c6) that also demonstrates some of the work from #16.

I'm bundling this as a PR to a PR #16 in hopes that it's a little easier to review 😄

title: Package Structure
description:
Awesome idea and really useful for classes that I teach.
I thought a package structure might be helpful, so I implemented one.
Although spread/gather is not yet implemented, this branch has a slightly different, yet powerful api as it allows the user to specify different datasets as well as the by-argument for joins.

One downside though is that the extra-joins (where multiple observations of y are added) are not yet correctly implemented. 

Do you think this will be helpful?

To give you a brief overview:

``` r
library(tidyAnimatedVerbs)
#> Loading required package: tidyverse
#> Loading required package: gganimate
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'tidyAnimatedVerbs'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:dplyr':
#> 
#>     combine

singer <- data_frame(name = c("Mick", "John", "Paul", "Matthew", "Mick"),
                     band = c("Stones", "Beatles", "Beatles", "Muse", "Foreigner"),
                     age  = c(75, 40, 76, 40, 73))

instr <- data_frame(name = c("Mick", "John", "Mick", "Keith"),
                    band = c("Stones", "Beatles", "Foreigner", "Stones"),
                    plays = c("guitar", "bass", "guitar", "guitar"))

singer
#> # A tibble: 5 x 3
#>   name    band        age
#>   <chr>   <chr>     <dbl>
#> 1 Mick    Stones       75
#> 2 John    Beatles      40
#> 3 Paul    Beatles      76
#> 4 Matthew Muse         40
#> 5 Mick    Foreigner    73

instr
#> # A tibble: 4 x 3
#>   name  band      plays 
#>   <chr> <chr>     <chr> 
#> 1 Mick  Stones    guitar
#> 2 John  Beatles   bass  
#> 3 Mick  Foreigner guitar
#> 4 Keith Stones    guitar

animate_left_join(singer, instr, by = c("name", "band"), text_size = 5)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/RYZXntp.gif)
